cases.sentence: Они испытывали оба одинаковое чувство, подобное тому, какое испытывает ученик после ___, оставшись в том же классе или навсегда исключенный из заведения.
cases.explain: «неудавшегося экзамена» — after the preposition «после», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: During the time of the children’s tea the grown-up people sat in the balcony and talked as though nothing had happened, though they all, especially Sergey Ivanovitch and Varenka, were very well aware that there had happened an event which, though negative, was of very great importance. They both had the same feeling, rather like that of a schoolboy after an examination, which has left him in the same class or shut him out of the school forever. Everyone present, feeling too that something had happened, talked eagerly about extraneous subjects. Levin and Kitty were particularly happy and conscious of their love that evening. And their happiness in their love seemed to imply a disagreeable slur on those who would have liked to feel the same and could not—and they felt a prick of conscience.

cases.explain: «посторонних предметах» — after the preposition «о», for location or topic.

cases.sentence: – Попомните мое слово: – Alexandre не приедет, – сказала ___.
cases.explain: «старая княгиня» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Mark my words, Alexander will not come,” said the old princess.

cases.sentence: Нынче вечером ждали с поезда Степана Аркадьича, и ___ писал, что, может быть, и он приедет.
cases.explain: «старый князь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: That evening they were expecting Stepan Arkadyevitch to come down by train, and the old prince had written that possibly he might come too.

cases.sentence: – Что вам, Агафья Михайловна? – спросила вдруг Кити остановившуюся с ___ и значительным лицом Агафью Михайловну.
cases.explain: «таинственным видом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: “What is it, Agafea Mihalovna?” Kitty asked suddenly of Agafea Mihalovna, who was standing with a mysterious air, and a face full of meaning.

cases.sentence: Варенька и в участливом ___ Левиных сумела быть полезною.
cases.explain: «благоустроенном доме» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Varenka was saying the same thing to Kitty. Even in the happy, well-ordered household of the Levins Varenka had succeeded in making herself useful.

cases.explain: «милая девушка» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “What a nice girl!” said the princess.

cases.sentence: Верно, папа! – прокричал Левин, остановившись у входа в аллею. – Кити, не ходи по ___, а кругом.
cases.explain: «крутой лестнице» — after the preposition «по», the dative marks the indirect object or recipient.
cases.translation: “And someone else too! Papa, of course!” cried Levin, stopping at the entrance of the avenue. “Kitty, don’t come down the steep staircase, go round.”

cases.sentence: Но Левин ошибся, приняв того, кто сидел в коляске, за ___.
cases.explain: «старого князя» — after the preposition «за», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: But Levin had been mistaken in taking the person sitting in the carriage for the old prince. As he got nearer to the carriage he saw beside Stepan Arkadyevitch not the prince but a handsome, stout young man in a Scotch cap, with long ends of ribbon behind. This was Vassenka Veslovsky, a distant cousin of the Shtcherbatskys, a brilliant young gentleman in Petersburg and Moscow society. “A capital fellow, and a keen sportsman,” as Stepan Arkadyevitch said, introducing him.

cases.sentence: Когда он приблизился к коляске, он увидал рядом со Степаном Аркадьичем не князя, а красивого полного молодого человека в ___ с длинными концами лент назади.
cases.explain: «шотландском колпачке» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
